messages:
Ashok (legal): Quick question from a prospective EU bank customer — they want BYOK but need to be sure key material never crosses borders. Also asking about export-control obligations (dual-use crypto) and the exact language we can put in the contract. Any guidance?

Maya (sec-eng): Short answer: we can support a deployment where key material never leaves the customer's chosen region. For Redwood Private we run the control plane in-customer-VPC or via a local on-prem package. HSMs stay in-region. :white_check_mark:

Paul (infra): To expand: we offer three patterns — 1) Customer-managed HSM in their cloud (CloudHSM/AzureHSM) with our agents talking to it, 2) On-prem HSM with PKCS#11 proxy, 3) Customer uploads a wrapped key material blob (import) into a regional KMS we run (only if they allow import). For patterns 1 & 2 the private key material never traverses Redwood owned infrastructure unencrypted.

Maya (sec-eng): From a compliance/export perspective: if the customer generates keys in-country (on an HSM) and never exports the unwrapped key, that meets most export-control and bank requirements. We should avoid wording that promises legal immunity — legal should use "Redwood will not export unwrapped customer key material outside the customer's selected region under normal operations."

Ashok (legal): Good. For contract language we need: 1) exact technical control description, 2) evidence (attestation + audit logs), 3) escalation if keys are requested by gov't. Can you sketch the evidence items we can produce?

Maya (sec-eng): Evidence we can provide: audit-trail of KMS operations (create/import/use/disable), HSM attestation output (manufacturer-signed quote/quote verification), network flow logs showing endpoints bound to region, and a signed runbook for key import/export procedures. Also ephemeral operator access logs (who requested, approved).

Sam (sre): On the logging side: for cloud HSMs we forward CloudTrail logs into a read-only, customer-owned S3 bucket or to their SIEM. For on-prem HSMs we can ship HSM audit-buffer extracts as signed bundles. Retention: customers can request retention policy in contract — typical regulated customers ask 7 years or "as required by local law."

Paul (infra): RBAC controls — recommend minimal roles: kms.viewer (readonly), kms.operator (rotate/rotate-wrap only), kms.importer (import token use), kms.admin (full). Import path should require 2-person approval (JIT CA via our console). We can support OIDC-based short-lived credentials for operators tied to SSO.

Maya (sec-eng): Additional safeguard: require import tokens to be single-use and time-bound. Also require wrap-with-customer-cmk for any transit wrapping so unwrapped material is never on our side.

Ashok (legal): Export-control note: if the key material is generated or imported inside a given country and is not moved in cleartext, do we still need to do anything special in the contract for dual-use cryptography?

Maya (sec-eng): Practically: describe the data flow (no unwrapped egress), the HSM attestation, and the operator access controls. If they want legal assurances beyond that (e.g., local certification), we flag it as a separate procurement/legal obligation.

Paul (infra): Quick technical example of an import flow we support (CLI):

```
# sample import (customer wraps key with import-token)
aws kms import-key-material \
  --key-id 1234abcd-12ab-34cd-56ef-1234567890ab \
  --encrypted-key-material fileb://wrapped.key \
  --import-token fileb://import_token.bin \
  --expiration-model KEY_MATERIAL_EXPIRES
```

Maya (sec-eng): Also call out: do NOT use generic cross-region replication for KMS configs for BYOK customers unless they explicitly consent. Replication would move key metadata (not raw unwrapped key) but we should be explicit in contract.

Sam (sre): Vulnerability triage note: if there's an HSM firmware vuln that requires an upgrade, we need a runbook: notify customer, present risk matrix (remote vs local exploit), schedule maintenance, and provide signed attestation of upgrade. For high-impact CVEs we should offer an escrow/rollback plan.

Ashok (legal): Good. Also need to define the "break glass" process: which authority can require us to transfer key material (court order) and how we will notify customer. Legal prefers a 24h notification window unless prohibited.

Maya (sec-eng): Operationally we can do: immediate legal intake, assess jurisdiction, if permitted we provide notice and a redacted summary. For Private deployments we expect to push back if the request would force key export. We'll add a clause: "We will notify customer of compelled disclosure unless prohibited by law."

deploy-bot: policy/pr-4567 merged — RBAC role names normalized to kms.viewer/operator/importer/admin.

audit-bot: audit:config-change by Maya (sec-eng) at 5109876702 — changed import-token TTL default from 24h to 2h.

Paul (infra): Action items: 1) Maya to draft the technical addendum (dataflow + attestation artifacts list), 2) Ashok to draft contract clause for "no export of unwrapped key material", 3) Sam to prepare maintenance & vuln response runbook for HSM firmware updates.

Maya (sec-eng): I'll put a short tech addendum in the compliance folder and ping legal. Will include sample logs and the import CLI snippet above. :thumbsup:

Ashok (legal): Thanks — if you can include a sample attestation bundle and sample notification template that would be ideal.

Maya (sec-eng): Will do.
